A fresh cut of beef, mutton or venison. Use it quickly, or salt it and smoke it.

A flask of clear water drawn straight from a spring. Alchemists swear it works better than well water.

A stoppered flask of clean water.

A small, sharpened iron point, ready to be fitted to an arrow shaft.

recipes.feat:
[color=#8e171c]Forgery (DC X)[/color] - This document appears genuine. A creature examining it must succeed on an Investigation check against DC X to notice it’s forged.

[color=#8e171c]Forged Documents[/color]
When you craft a Forged Document, choose its type and make a crafting roll. Forgeries follow these rules:

[color=#8e171c]Document Type[/color]: Each type of document draws on a different skill:
Personal Letter: Persuasion
Writ of Passage: Deception
Legal Document: Lore
Royal Decree: Lore

[color=#8e171c]Crafting Roll[/color]: Roll a d20 and add your Scribing Rank and your Rank in the document’s associated skill. The total becomes the document’s Forgery DC.
[color=#8e171c]No Failure[/color]: The document is always completed. A low roll simply makes a poor forgery, and anyone who looks closely may see through it.
[color=#8e171c]Official Seal[/color]: A Royal Decree also requires an Official Seal as a material.
recipes.quote: “I don’t forge documents. I write the letters the guard captain would have written, had he been a more reasonable man.” -Oswin Quillfeather

recipes.feat: Livingwood - This weapon weighs half as much, never rots or warps, and mends itself of mundane damage over a long rest. This feature doesn’t take up a modifier slot.
recipes.quote: “Humans shape their bows. Elves grow ours, and only finish what the tree began.” -Faelan Ashgrove

recipes.feat: Picking - You can use a lockpick to make a Thievery check to open a lock. If the check fails, the lockpick breaks and can’t be used again. Without a lockpick or a similar tool, you can’t attempt to pick a lock.
recipes.quote: “I make locks and I make lockpicks. People ask if that’s a conflict of interest. I tell them it’s job security.” -Wendle Cogsworth

recipes.grants: Enchanted: Luminous, fills 1 open modifier slot
recipes.feat:
Luminous - As a free action, you can speak this weapon’s Command Word to make it shed bright light in a 20 ft. radius and dim light for an additional 20 ft., or speak it again to stop.

[color=#8e171c]Enchantment Modifiers[/color]
An Enchantment Modifier is a Craftable Modifier that can only be crafted by a character who can cast spells, using an Enchantment Table. It’s applied to an existing item listed in its Applies To line, fills one of that item’s open modifier slots, and gives the item the Enchanted property.

[color=#8e171c]Command Words[/color]
Some enchantments are activated by speaking a Command Word. When you craft an Enchantment Modifier that requires one, you choose its Command Word, which can be any word or short phrase. Command Words follow these rules:

[color=#8e171c]Activation[/color]: A creature holding or wearing the item can speak the Command Word to activate it. Speaking a Command Word is a free action (costs 0AP) unless the enchantment says otherwise.

[color=#8e171c]Knowing the Word[/color]: Only creatures who know the Command Word can activate the enchantment. The enchanter can share it with anyone they choose, or keep it secret.

[color=#8e171c]Speaking Required[/color]: A creature that can’t speak, such as one that is Muted, can’t activate a Command Word.
recipes.quote: “Every apprentice’s first enchantment is light. Not because it’s easy, but because a mage who can’t see in the dark doesn’t stay a mage for long.” -Aelindra Moonweave

recipes.feat: Restorative - A creature that drinks this regains 1d6 + 1 hit points.
recipes.quote: “It tastes like a cellar floor, and it’ll close a wound before you finish complaining about the taste. Medicine was never meant to be pleasant.” -Isolde Vexmire

recipes.feat: Slumbering - A humanoid that drinks this must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or fall Unconscious for 1 hour. The creature wakes early if it takes damage or another creature uses an action to shake it awake. The brew is colorless and nearly tasteless when mixed into another drink.
recipes.quote: “Surface folk fear our blades, but the Matriarchs have never needed blades. A cup of wine, a quiet toast, and by morning a rival is simply… gone. The deep has always preferred patience to steel.” -Ilvane Mournshade, Dark Elf Apothecary
“Knights brag about their plate, but ask them what’s underneath. It’s my stitching keeping them alive.” -Mirra Threadwell
“Paper is for shopping lists. Parchment is for words that need to outlive the one who wrote them.” -Oswin Quillfeather
“A walking stick for the road, and a reason to keep walking for anyone who’d stop you.” -Tobin Burrowbark
“Goose for letters, crow for fine lines, and never, ever a griffon. They come back for their feathers.” -Oswin Quillfeather

recipes.pre: +3 Enchanting, Spellcasting, Arcane Major or Minor: Abjuration
recipes.grants: Enchanted: Resist 1, or Resist 2 on TC, fills 1 open modifier slot
recipes.feat: Resist X - When you take mundane damage, reduce that damage by X. You can only benefit from the Resist property on one piece of equipment at a time.
recipes.quote: “Ah, I see Mister Thorne has been listening to last week’s lecture. Yes, for those of you worried about that orc’s axe, there is an answer. It costs twice as much silver, and you’ll still feel it. Heh heh.” -Professor Aurelian Silverscale, Lecturer of Abjuration

recipes.applies: Any weapon with the Thrown property
recipes.grants: Enchanted: Returning, fills 1 open modifier slot
recipes.feat: Returning - After you make a ranged attack with this weapon, it flies back to your hand at the end of your turn.
recipes.quote: “An axe that comes home is the only kind of loyalty some warriors ever know.” -Aelindra Moonweave
“A seal says two things: who sent the letter, and that no one else has read it. Only one of those is ever true.” -Oswin Quillfeather

recipes.pre: +3 Enchanting, Spellcasting, Arcane Major or Minor: Evocation
recipes.grants: Enchanted: Searing 1, or Searing 2 on TC, fills 1 open modifier slot
recipes.feat: Searing X - This weapon deals an additional X magical fire damage on a hit.
recipes.quote: “Fire is not a weapon, my friends. Fire is a passion! We simply teach it where to go. And please, no more practicing near the mustache.” -Professor Vigo Brasamonte, Lecturer of Evocation
“Yew remembers the shape you give it. Be kind to it, and it’ll be kind to your aim.” -Tobin Burrowbark
“Smiths make arrowheads by the hundred. I make ten, and every one of them has an appointment with something that should’ve stayed dead.” -Lucien Gilt
“A hundred little links, each one holding the next. Not unlike a good adventuring party, though the chain complains less.” -Lucien Gilt

recipes.feat: Sacred - This item counts as a holy symbol for any spell or feature that requires one.
recipes.quote: “I don’t pray. But I’ve made symbols for a dozen gods, and I’ll admit some of them feel warmer in the hand than others.” -Lucien Gilt
“A plain silver ring is a promise waiting to be made. Enchanters see an empty vessel. Lovers see a question. Both pay well.” -Lucien Gilt
“Everything beautiful I’ve ever made started as a thread of silver thinner than a hair, and the patience to not snap it.” -Lucien Gilt

recipes.feat:
[color=#8e171c]Silvered[/color] - This weapon counts as silver for overcoming resistances and vulnerabilities, such as those of lycanthropes, certain fiends, and aberrations.

[color=#8e171c]Craftable Modifiers[/color]
A Craftable Modifier doesn’t create a new item. Instead, it’s applied to an existing item listed in its Applies To line, filling one of that item’s open modifier slots. If the item has no open slots, the modifier can’t be applied.
recipes.quote: “Bring me your blade, and I’ll give it a conscience. Werewolves hate a weapon with principles.” -Lucien Gilt
“Every blade in the world is only as good as the hand holding it, and the handle holding the blade.” -Tobin Burrowbark
"Small buckles hold sheaths, pouches, and belts. Small work, sure, but a dropped coin purse has started more bar fights than any insult." -Molly Stoneheart

recipes.feat: Rousing - Holding this under the nose of a creature within 5 ft. ends the Dazed condition, or wakes it if it’s Unconscious but has at least 1 hit point.
recipes.quote: “A single whiff will wake a sleeping ogre. I know this because I’ve tested it. I don’t recommend testing it.” -Isolde Vexmire

recipes.feat:
Preserved - This food doesn’t spoil for 2 weeks and can be eaten during a rest or at camp without a Cooking Fire.

Quick Bite - You can eat this outside of a rest by spending 1 AP, regaining hit points equal to the cook’s Cooking Rank. A creature can only benefit from one Quick Bite between rests.
recipes.quote: “Hardtack fills your belly at camp. Jerky’s what you chew on while something is chasing you. Smart adventurers carry both.” -Bram Copperpot

recipes.matNote: plus the spell’s own material component
recipes.feat:
Scroll - When you craft this, choose one spell you know, one language you know, and the scroll’s Rank (X). X can’t exceed your Scribing Tier’s maximum or your own Rank in that spell. If you meet the TC, X increases by 1. The spell is written into the scroll in that language. A spellcaster who knows the language can read the scroll to cast the spell, following the Spell Scroll rules. You must be capable of casting the spell in order to copy it to a scroll.

[color=#8e171c]Naming Convention for Scrolls[/color]
Spell Scrolls are named by their Rank, language, and spell, such as a [color=#8e171c]+1 Dwarvish Spell Scroll of Firebolt[/color].

[color=#8e171c]Spell Scrolls[/color]
A spellcaster can read a Spell Scroll to cast the spell stored in it, even if they don’t know that spell or aren’t high enough level to learn it. Reading a scroll follows these rules:

[color=#8e171c]Class[/color]: Your class must be listed in the spell’s Class Requirements.
[color=#8e171c]Language[/color]: You must know the language the scroll was written in.
[color=#8e171c]Cost[/color]: You pay the spell’s normal casting cost, using MP or AP in place of MP.
[color=#8e171c]Rank[/color]: The spell is cast at the Rank listed on the scroll, using your own spellcasting modifier.
[color=#8e171c]Overreaching[/color]: If the spell’s Level is higher than your character level, you gain Exhaustion Points equal to the difference after the spell resolves.
[color=#8e171c]Single Use[/color]: The scroll crumbles to ash once read.
[color=#8e171c]Magic[/color]: Spell Scrolls count as magic items.

[color=#8e171c]Scribing Tiers → Scroll Rank[/color]
Basic: Up to +3 or less
Advance: Up to +6 or less
Mastery: Up to +10 or less

[color=#8e171c]Magical Scribing[/color]
Scribing recipes that involve spells, such as spell scrolls or copying spells into a spellbook, can only be crafted by a character who can cast spells.
recipes.quote: “A scroll is a spell asleep on a page. Wake it gently, and only when you mean it. And never, ever wake one you aren’t ready for.” -Oswin Quillfeather

recipes.feat: Warming - A creature that eats this has advantage on saving throws against extreme cold until its next rest or camp.
recipes.quote: “Half the dungeons out there are colder than a dwarf’s handshake. A bowl of this before you go down, and you’ll feel the peppers long after you’ve forgotten the cold.” -Bram Copperpot
“Every hedge-wizard who’s ever singed their eyebrows casting Firebolt owes me for the powder. Most of them never pay.” -Isolde Vexmire

recipes.feat:
Preserved - This food doesn’t spoil for 2 weeks and can be eaten at camp or during a rest without a Cooking Fire.

Nourishing - A creature that eats this during a rest or at camp regains hit points equal to the cook’s Cooking Rank.
recipes.quote: “It won’t win you any friends at the table, but it’ll keep you alive long enough to find a better one. Every adventurer who’s laughed at my hardtack has come back for more.” -Bram Copperpot

recipes.pre: +3 Enchanting, Spellcasting, Arcane Major or Minor: Abjuration
recipes.grants: Enchanted: Warding 1, or Warding 2 on TC, fills 1 open modifier slot
recipes.feat: Warding X - When you take magical damage from a spell or other magical source, reduce that damage by X. You can only benefit from the Warding property on one piece of equipment at a time.
recipes.quote: “Now, class, Warding will turn aside a fair bit of a fireball, a lightning bolt, or a hex hurled by a jealous rival. What it won’t do is stop an ordinary orc with an ordinary axe from rearranging your ordinary ribs. Magic is polite enough to knock first. Steel never is. Heh heh.” -Professor Aurelian Silverscale, Lecturer of Abjuration

recipes.feat: Whisperweave - This piece weighs nothing, makes no sound as you move, and can't be torn, stained, or soiled by mundane means. This feature doesn't take up a modifier slot.
recipes.quote: “There is one rule in the deep, older than the Matriarchs and colder than the stone: whoever is heard first, dies first. Every step I stitch into these soles is a step you’ll never have to explain to something hungry.” -Viscara Duskthread

recipes.feat: Whisperweave - This piece weighs nothing, makes no sound as you move, and can't be torn, stained, or soiled by mundane means. This feature doesn't take up a modifier slot.
recipes.quote: “Surface folk think the dark is empty, so they fill it with torches and noise. We learned to wear it instead. A good hood doesn’t hide your face, child. It convinces the dark you were never there at all.” -Viscara Duskthread

recipes.feat: Whisperweave - This piece weighs nothing, makes no sound as you move, and can't be torn, stained, or soiled by mundane means. This feature doesn't take up a modifier slot.
recipes.quote: “The broodmothers spin silk stronger than steel and lighter than breath, and they never once thought to make armor of it. My grandmother did. She spent forty years learning to take it from them without being eaten, and every thread in this mantle is a lesson she survived.” -Viscara Duskthread
“Wrap it tight, seal it with resin, and a sweaty palm won’t cost you your sword arm.” -Hollis Tanworth
